verses.1: And the shadow of Jehovah was in the fields of Philistines for seven years.
verses.2: And the Philistines called the priests and the scribes, and said, “What will happen to the ark of God? Do you know where we are being sent?”
verses.3: And they said, “If you send out the ark of the God of Israel, then do not send it away empty. For when He returns, He will restore it to its place. Then you will be healed. And I will tell you why your hands are not allowed to touch him.”
verses.4: And they said, “What are those curses that have been placed upon him?” They also said, “According to the calculations of the Philistines, there are five gold rings and five silver bracelets for each one of them. And these are all part of their punishment.”
verses.5: And you made idols of your idols and of your worthless images, who destroy the land. You showed honor to the gods of Israel, but I will humble their hands over you, over your gods, and over your land.
verses.6: And why do you be sad when you are freed from Egypt? Why do you not rejoice, since Pharaoh had treated you badly and sent you away?
verses.7: And now, make a new wheel. Also, take two fruits that haven’t been used before. Place these fruits on the wheel. Then, put them back in their proper places.
verses.8: And you took the Ark of God, and you placed it in the chariot. And all the gold objects that were inside it, you put them into a basket beside it. Then you sent it away.
verses.9: And if you see that the path along its border leads to the house of Shem, then it has done us this great harm. But if we don’t know that it never actually touched us, then it was still a harm to us.
verses.10: And the people did as they were told. They took two ripe apples, put them in a basket, and ate them inside the house.
verses.11: And they set the chariots of Yahweh in place, along with the golden shields and the golden trumpets.
verses.12: And the women walked along the road leading to Bet Shemesh. They continued walking, but they didn’t turn right or left. The Philistines followed behind them, all the way to the border of Bet Shemesh.
verses.13: And in the field where they harvested wheat, they stood in the thick darkness. They raised their eyes and saw the grain. They were happy to see it.
verses.14: And the serpent came to Jehosua’s field, to Bethel-Shimshai. There, it stood on a large rock. They cut off the branches of the serpent and carried them up to Jehovah.
verses.15: And the Levites removed the Ark of God and the golden vessels that were in it. They placed them on the large stone altar. And the people of the house of God offered sacrifices to God on that day.
verses.16: And five of the Philistines saw this, and they returned to their homes that day.
verses.17: And these are the treasures of gold that the Philistines returned to Jehovah. One for Ashdod, one for Gaza, one for Ashkelon, one for Gat, and one for Ekron.
verses.18: And the treasures of gold were counted from all the cities of the Philistines. They included five throngs of people from the city of Mizraim, all the way to Kefar Prazhi. There was also the great altar on which the Ark of God was placed until today, in the field of Joshua, at Bethel-Shimshai.
verses.19: And there was great sorrow among the people of Bet Shemesh, because they saw the ark of God. There were seventy men, each with fifty thousand men. The people mourned greatly, for God had struck the people with a great disaster.
verses.20: And they said, “Who can stand before the LORD, the Holy God? And who can rise above us?”
verses.21: And they sent angels to the inhabitants of the forests, saying, “Let the Philistines take back the Ark of God. Bring it back to you.”
